I drove two complete anonymous loops against the hosted instance (4.82s and 4.86s vs a claimed ~4.5s): skin scores with the lowest one named as the priority area, a colour read whose detected hex values match a committed receipt, a garment selected by that undertone and rendered onto the photo, a lighting pass, a horizon-aware countdown, and an eight-row priced cross-category basket. The special-category chain is not narrated, it is watchable: two faces produced two colour reads and two different garment renders on their own photos. The ledger read 0/8 before and 0/8 after; no unit was spent. The strongest evidence in the repo is a hash chain I reproduced myself: the relight the live site serves == the repo fixture == `receipts/002/photo_lighting.render.jpg`, sha256 `2823726249d36b58…`, a genuine Perfect Corp task. The images a judge looks at literally ARE the provider's output. The judge code works (303 + HttpOnly cookie), `/api/dev/verify` is 401 anonymous and 200 authed at zero units, replaying real task_ids, real `/s2s/v2.x/task/...` endpoints, and — to their credit — the failure `error_src_face_too_small`, alongside a self-authored caveat that the four-step chain has never completed in one live run. The required technology is genuine, non-trivial, first-party integration code that is deliberately dormant for public visitors behind a gate rather than a silent flag, and the product says so in four separate places on screen. The verdict turns on delivery, not engineering. `submission/devpost.md` is still self-labelled "(DRAFT)", is not pasted into Devpost, and its Testing instructions still hold the literal placeholder `<PASTE THE JUDGE CODE HERE>` — so a judge opening Devpost today most likely sees no entry, and even a verbatim paste would hand them no working access code. The 88.44s voiced demo reel exists, is compliant, and is gitignored and uploaded nowhere; their own COMPLIANCE.md calls this the last hard blocker and correctly notes a VPS-hosted file does not satisfy the rule. There is still no architecture or fusion diagram, and no CI. Four adversarial findings the docs do not currently own: the agentic engine is degraded right now (`key_present_unverified`, probe aborted, `degraded: true` on three consecutive reads) while CLAIM_PROOF_MAP still asserts it reports `live` — the "two engines" differentiator is presently unwitnessable by anyone; README:193 and devpost:97 still say the sample path credits "three APIs, not four" when the live wedding run renders four and their own screenshot says four, so the copy now contradicts itself and undersells the product; the selfie file input is still `className="hidden"`, so a keyboard-only judge cannot upload a photo (review 001 flagged this, it is unfixed, and the sample buttons are what save the demo); and `lib/live/ledger.ts` fails open by design, meaning an unreadable ledger file would silently disable the 8-run spend cap while still reporting the reassuring 0/8 I relied on. Nothing here is fabricated — the copy is hedged, the gaps are self-documented, failures are committed rather than hidden, and CLAIM_PROOF_MAP volunteers unreconciled unit spend that cuts against the author. This is a finished engine behind an unopened showroom, three days from the 2026-08-17 deadline, with the newest adversarial review (30/50, Stage One FAIL) predating the four best improvements in the build.

judges.judge: YouCam API Team — Technological Implementation lens (Perfect Corp reviewer)
judges.one_line_verdict: The best integration code I have seen this track, wired into a chain I could actually watch propagate — skin score to countdown to basket, undertone to garment to render — but every reachable path returns a fingerprint-keyed replay before the endpoint is even resolved, so what the running product proves is a very honest recording, not a live integration.
judges.fatal_flaw: No judge can witness a single live YouCam call, and the fused chain has never once completed live — their own words. All six feature modules open with `if (fixturesActive()) return fixture…(input)`, so the endpoint is never resolved on any public path; the one live path is welded to `claimLiveRun()` against an 8-run budget, so it cannot be demoed safely even with the code I was given; the LLM engine that is supposed to do the orchestrating reports `key_present_unverified` / probe aborted / `degraded: true` on every probe, so half the pitch is unwitnessable by anyone today; and `/api/dev/verify` carries its own caveat that the bundled wedding selfie is rejected by BOTH analysis APIs (`error_src_face_too_small`), meaning the four-step fused run my 9-10 band describes has literally never happened. Of 8 declared APIs, `lookVto` has zero call sites and makeup/hairstyle 401 — the real number is 4, and `/healthz` still leads a skimming judge with 8. The receipts and the byte-identical hash chain are excellent evidence, but they are artifacts; my criterion asks the running product, and the running product replays. Compounding it from the delivery side: the 88s video is on no host and the Devpost entry is unfiled with `<PASTE THE JUDGE CODE HERE>` still literal in the testing field, so today this engine has an audience of zero.
judges.flip_to_champion: Spend two of your eight units to make one live end-to-end four-step run exist, then let me watch one. COMPLIANCE.md already contains your own measured table of which images the API accepts as a face — swap the bundled wedding selfie for one of those, capture the first run where skin → colour → cloth-v3 → lighting all succeed on the same photo, commit that receipt, and delete the caveat. Then give the unlocked judge the configuration you never deployed: your route already handles `unlocked && env.youcamFixtures`, so ship a single "run this one live" button that streams the four real task_ids into the provenance ledger as they arrive, timestamped, next to the replayed contract. One live run, visible on screen, converts my 7 to a 9 and your tiebreaker 8 to a 10 — and it is the hero beat your video currently cannot show. Precondition, because nothing else scores without it: upload the reel to YouTube and file the entry with a real judge code.
judges.presentation_note: The artifacts are 8-grade and the delivery is 2-grade, and I can only score what reaches me. CLAIM_PROOF_MAP.md is the best governance document in this track — measured rows naming the command that produced each number, an explicit "not yet measured" section, and a "known contradictions" section that volunteers unreconciled unit spend against its own author. Committed receipts carry genuine 100+ character Perfect Corp task_ids and, to their credit, the failures. I reproduced the hash chain myself: the relight the live site serves is byte-identical to `receipts/002/photo_lighting.render.jpg`, so the image I looked at literally IS Perfect Corp's output. That is exactly the falsifiable artifact this criterion rewards. Then it all sits in a drawer. No hosted video, no filed entry, no architecture or fusion diagram anywhere in the tree — and the tiebreaker is literally about the chain being SEEN, so the one missing visual is the one that would have carried it. No CI. And there is live claim-to-proof drift of precisely the kind that costs points: README:193 and devpost:97 still say the sample path credits "three APIs, not four" while the product renders four and your own screenshot says four — you are underselling your single strongest asset in the copy a judge skims; CLAIM_PROOF_MAP asserts `agentic_engine: live` when it reports `key_present_unverified`; the revision row is stale at 1cb7784 against a live 90915ab; COMPLIANCE says nine screenshots and there are ten. The video itself, which I extracted frames from, is genuinely good — real product footage, a persistent "demo mode · captured YouCam renders · 0 API units" badge burned in, a drag-compare of the actual VTO render, the $724 basket with a budget fitter, and beat b9 is a real self-catch ("hand it a photo it has never seen and it refuses instead of showing you a stranger"). It has no live-firing hero beat and no measured tester delta, and nobody on earth can watch it. Given only the video and the submission page, a judge could confirm nothing — because neither exists yet.

judges.judge: YouCam API Team — Design lens (Perfect Corp)
judges.one_line_verdict: The only entry in the track whose edges are actually built — real skipped/failed chip states, honest empty states, sticky mobile checkout, aria-live on the stream — and then it hands a keyboard user no way in and puts the wrong garment in the hero frame of its own payoff screen.
judges.fatal_flaw: The deliverable contradicts itself in its single most important frame. `components/Concierge.tsx:617` sets `heroUrl = state.images.finish ?? state.images.apparel`, so the relight outranks the try-on: on the wedding sample the look board's editorial hero is the man standing in his own t-shirt and joggers, captioned 'Occasion lighting · rendered by YouCam AI', six centimetres from copy that says 'dress you in the Slate Blue Three-Piece Suit' — and the suit render exists, demoted to the evidence grid below. Screenshot 05-countdown.jpg ships that contradiction into the gallery. This is exactly the slot where a fourth stranger's photo used to live; the identity fix was right, but it swapped a truth bug for a coherence bug and nobody re-looked at the frame. Compounding it, the one control that makes the look yours is unreachable: the selfie `<input type="file">` is still `className="hidden"` inside a bare label (line 1481), so a keyboard-only visitor is confined to two bundled strangers — flagged in review 001, unfixed — and 'keyboard reachable' is the first thing I check. A product that says 'from one selfie' must let me give it mine, and must show me wearing the thing it just told me to wear.
judges.flip_to_champion: Fix the payoff frame and the way in, in that order: make the apparel render the look-board hero (relight becomes supporting evidence, and when no render exists for that person show the honest empty state rather than an image of the wrong outfit), and replace the hidden file input with a real focusable control — a visible `<button>` that calls `inputRef.current.click()`, input kept off-screen with `sr-only` instead of `hidden` so it stays in the accessibility tree. That is a two-line change and a ten-line change, and together they turn 'beautiful happy path' into 'finished product': every screenshot, the video's hero beat and the Devpost gallery would then show the garment the plan promised, on a photo the judge supplied with the keyboard. Ship one 320px screenshot of the look board alongside them and I would argue for this entry on design.
judges.presentation_note: The live product presents itself better than the submission does — the announcement bar, the provenance ledger's 'Nothing was called just now', and the hash-chained receipts are the most trustworthy self-presentation in this track, and I verified the loop myself in under three seconds. But a Devpost judge receives none of it: the entry is not filed, the 88 s voiced cut is gitignored and hosted nowhere, and the testing field still literally reads '<PASTE THE JUDGE CODE HERE>', so the access code that makes the gated paths inspectable reaches no one. From my lens the specific presentation failure is that all ten stills are desktop-width and there is no narrow-viewport frame anywhere in the repo — the code shows careful mobile work (sticky checkout summary, flex-wrap rows, min-w-0 discipline) and the submission proves none of it, which is how a genuinely responsive build gets scored as a desktop demo. There is also still no architecture or fusion diagram, which is unforgivable when the declared tiebreaker is literally about the chain being seen, and two prose sentences (README:193, devpost:97) now undersell the product at 'three APIs, not four' while the shipped screenshot says four. The honesty apparatus is grand-prize grade; the delivery is unshipped, and today that reads as slideware to anyone who cannot clone the repo.

Run them at 21 days out and again the day before, capture their actual YouCam skin scores both times, and render that on the results screen and at the very top of the Devpost page: "Marta — wedding 5 Sept — dark circles 59 → 71 over 21 days on this plan, YouCam-measured, receipts committed." That one row does four things at once: it names the audience my criterion demands, it converts every asserted impact claim into evidence, it fills the measured-number slot the 5th criterion is currently empty on, and it becomes the first genuine first-party signal a retailer would actually want — a scored before/after tied to a dated purchase intent. Then file the entry and put the video on YouTube. I would champion that version; I cannot champion an empty audience field.
judges.presentation_note: The depth is real and the honesty apparatus is the best I have seen in this track — CLAIM_PROOF_MAP.md volunteers evidence against its own author, failures are committed rather than hidden, and I reproduced the hash chain myself: the relight the live site serves is byte-identical to receipts/002, so the images I looked at literally ARE Perfect Corp output. judges.judge: YouCam API Team — Quality of the Idea lens (Perfect Corp reviewer)
judges.one_line_verdict: The one genuinely non-obvious idea here — an LLM turning our skin scores into a plan whose KIND changes with how many days are left — is the one thing no judge can watch happen, and the rule-based engine that judges do reach cannot parse a date.
judges.fatal_flaw: The wedge is asserted, not demonstrated — and the fallback fails at the task the product is named for. Your pitch is "you tell it the event AND THE DATE" and an LLM plans around the time available. On every path I could reach, no LLM plans anything: /healthz returned agentic_engine "key_present_unverified", agentic_engine_reason "This operation was aborted", degraded true on every probe I made, so the reasoning layer is currently unwitnessable by anyone — code, receipts and prompt notwithstanding. That leaves lib/concierge/deterministic.ts, a regex plus a rule table, as the only planner a judge sees. I typed the most natural input a real user would type — "my sister-in-law vow renewal on the beach, 2026-08-16", two days out — and the hosted instance returned daysUntil: null, a three-week countdown, and the sentence "I planned for about three weeks — tell me the date for a tighter countdown." I had given the date. lib/concierge/occasion.ts parseDays() has no calendar branch at all: it handles "in N days/weeks", tonight/tomorrow, next week/month, this/next weekend and weekday names, and nothing else — no ISO date, no "August 16", no "the 16th". Same run also picked a Scarlet A-Line Gown for a beach ceremony because "vow renewal" matches none of the seven occasion aliases, so type fell through to undefined. So the two words of your own pitch — "name an occasion", "and the date" — are exactly the two places the reachable engine breaks, and your own anti-pattern note says the product must be "the plan for a specific day." With supported phrasing ("in 2 days") the horizon logic is genuinely good and switches the plan in kind ("no skincare changes this close"), which makes this more painful, not less: the insight is real and the input path to it is a keyhole. Against my loss condition — novelty asserted rather than demonstrated — this lands squarely.
judges.flip_to_champion: Make the planning visible and make the date real, in that order. (1) Ship a committed, keyless, zero-unit replay of ONE agentic run — the same occasion and selfie sent through both engines, rendered side by side on the live site, so I can see the LLM reorder the countdown, justify the garment against the undertone, and get the cut guard in agent-tools.ts to bounce a bad pick and re-choose. That diff between the two plans IS your idea; today it exists only in prose. Ten seconds of watching it would move me from 6 to 9, because the tool-error-as-constraint-solver pattern (try_on_apparel returning is_error so the model must re-pick a cut that respects what the shopper actually said, rather than inferring gender from the photo) is a use of our API our own docs would never suggest, and I have no way to see it fire. (2) Add ~15 lines of calendar parsing plus a date field beside the occasion box so "2026-08-16" and "August 16" resolve to a 2-day horizon, and widen the occasion aliases past seven. Right now your placeholder text ("An evening wedding in 3 weeks") is teaching users to phrase around a parser gap, and the product's headline promise silently degrades into the generic three-week default the moment they don't.
judges.presentation_note: The depth is real and the submission does not deliver it. CLAIM_PROOF_MAP.md is the best governance artifact I have read in this track — every number bound to the command that produced it, an explicit "not yet measured" section, and a "known contradictions still open" section that volunteers unreconciled unit spend against its own author. The receipts are real: I re-hashed the relight the live site serves against receipts/002 and got the same sha256 (2823726249d36b58…), so the image a judge looks at literally is Perfect Corp's output, and /api/dev/verify volunteers its own caveat that the four-step chain has never completed in one live run plus the genuine wire detail that the url appears one poll before task_status flips to success — that is scar tissue a fabricator does not invent. And then: the 88s voiced video is on no host, so nobody can watch it; the Devpost entry is unfiled three days from the deadline; the testing field still literally reads "<PASTE THE JUDGE CODE HERE>", meaning even a verbatim paste hands me no way into the gated paths; there is still no architecture or fusion diagram anywhere, when the tiebreaker is precisely about the chain being SEEN; and no CI. Two stale sentences (README:193, devpost:97) now claim three APIs when the live wedding run renders four and your own screenshot says four — you are underselling yourselves in writing. The hosted keyless demo is genuinely excellent and one-click, which is the only reason this is a 4 and not a 2. But the artifact that carries an idea-quality claim is the video, and yours is a file on a laptop.

judges.judge: YouCam API Team — Perfect Corp, Special category lens: Skin AI and Apparel VTO as one experience
judges.one_line_verdict: The countdown is visibly driven by the skin read and that half of the fusion is real and watchable in one run — but the garment half is a tiebreaker worth half of formality, it is absent on the very path I clicked first, and the only run where it shows lives in a video on no host and in none of the ten screenshots.
judges.fatal_flaw: On the wedding preset — the hero path, the only one with a full-body try-on and all four APIs — the skin reading demonstrably does NOT determine the garment, and the video says it does. Live, the colour API returned warm / Warm Spring; the chosen slate-suit is marked flatters: \"cool\" in the author's own catalogue (catalog.ts:100). The picker weights undertone 2 against formality 4 (deterministic.ts:358-372), and the masculine cut filter collapses 11 garments to one viable option, so the reading is arithmetically incapable of choosing. The product is honest about it — garmentColorClause correctly emits nothing, and my run's line was just \"right for a wedding\" with no colour reasoning anywhere. But narration beat b3 plays over that exact run asserting \"that reading is what chooses the garment.\" So the one sentence that sells my category is narrated over the one run where it is false. Their own /api/dev/verify concedes the rest: \"The fused chain has never completed in one live run.\" And the fusion that IS real — two faces, two colour reads, two different garments on their own photos, which I did reproduce live (warm/masculine to slate-suit, cool to sky-wrap-maxi with the render at /fixtures/apparel-sky-maxi.jpg) — appears in zero of the ten committed screenshots and only in beat b6 of a reel that is gitignored and uploaded nowhere. Fusion that exists in code, is half-visible on one of two paths, and is proven in no artifact a judge can open.
judges.flip_to_champion: Put the causal edge on screen and make the hero path be the two-face comparison. One view, side by side: the same occasion, two selfies, each panel showing its detected skin hex and undertone, an explicit \"why this garment\" chip naming the garment's flatters value against the read undertone, and the two different YouCam renders beneath. When they disagree — warm read, cool suit, because only one masculine cut exists — say that out loud in the chip; the honesty is a feature and it turns the weakest moment into the most trustworthy one. That converts the flat four-chip ApiLedger from \"which APIs ran\" into \"which reading produced which garment,\" which is the whole criterion. Then upload the reel with b6 as the opening beat and ship one still of that comparison into the gallery. That is a UI beat and two uploads, not a rebuild, and it would move my tiebreaker from 6 to a 9.
judges.presentation_note: The depth is real and the artifacts that exist are unusually good — I reproduced the hash chain myself (live /fixtures/finish-wedding.jpg == repo == receipts/002/photo_lighting.render.jpg, sha256 2823726249d36b58…), so the images I looked at literally ARE Perfect Corp output, which is the strongest single proof in this submission and better than most teams manage. presentation.verdict: A finished, well-evidenced engine behind an unopened showroom. Two of the three pillars this criterion weighs — a watchable demo video and a filed submission page — do not exist for a judge today, three days from the deadline. The third pillar, the linked artifacts, is genuinely strong to exemplary: I independently reproduced the receipt-to-live hash chain (Perfect Corp receipt 002 sha256 2823726249d36b58… == public/fixtures/finish-wedding.jpg == the bytes the live site serves), which is a 9-10-grade falsifiable trust artifact a competitor structurally cannot fake without real provider calls. /api/dev/verify answers 401 anonymous and 200 with the judge cookie at units_spent_by_this_request: 0, replaying real /s2s/v2.x endpoints, genuine 100+ char task_ids, and — to their credit — the failure error_src_face_too_small plus a self-authored caveat that the fused chain has never completed live. The hosted loop is keyless and drivable (I measured 4.42 s; ledger read 0/8 before and 0/8 after, unchanged). CLAIM_PROOF_MAP.md is the best governance artifact I have seen in this repo class: ~40 measured rows each naming its command, a "Not yet measured — and said so out loud" section, and a "Known contradictions still open" section that volunteers unreconciled unit spend cutting against the author. That apparatus is what keeps this out of the 1-3 slideware band decisively. But the criterion is about what a skimming, skeptical judge can verify without trusting the author, and today they can verify nothing through the channel that matters. The 88.4 s voiced cut is gitignored (.gitignore:52-53), tracked by no host (git ls-files submission/ returns zero mp4s; config.json videoUrl reads "NOT UPLOADED"), so Stage One kill gate 4 and COMPLIANCE row 6 both fail on it — and the 5-6 band explicitly presumes "it would pass Stage One". Nothing here is dishonest — the gaps are self-documented, failures are committed rather than hidden, and the vocabulary law is clean with zero banned-word hits. verdict.bottom_line: OFFICIAL: 33/50, up 3 from review 002's 30. STAGE ONE: FAIL, for the third consecutive review, on the same two rows. DEPTH & PRESENTATION (diagnostic, not folded in): 4.0/10, up 0.5 from 3.5. All five lanes reported; none failed. Aphrodite is now a genuinely finished, deployed, honestly-labelled product with the best evidence apparatus this panel has seen in the track — and it has an audience of zero. The engineering improvements since 2026-08-10 are real and I verified them rather than trusting them: the receipt-to-fixture-to-live-served sha256 chain reproduces (2823726249d36b58… three ways), two faces visibly produce two colour reads and two different YouCam renders in one run, /api/dev/verify replays real Perfect Corp task_ids at zero units including a committed failure, 117 tests pass with no setup, and the deploy provably matches HEAD. CLAIM_PROOF_MAP volunteers evidence against its own author, which is the single most trust-earning artifact here. None of that reaches a judge. The video is on no host (I re-ran the grep: zero URLs), the Devpost entry is unfiled with the judge code still a literal placeholder, and — new, verified live by me — POST /api/unlock 303s to https://localhost:3100/, so even a judge holding the code lands on a dead page. Three findings also cut against the honesty story the project stakes itself on and must be fixed before submitting, not after: public/fixtures/apparel-suit.jpg is the first render a judge sees and its stated receipt provenance fails the hash check (739192e8… vs receipt 000's 27c9d899…, file committed three weeks before the run it cites); CLAIM_PROOF_MAP:72 asserts agentic_engine 'live' when it reads key_present_unverified, degraded, on every probe; and narration beats b3 and b5 assert that the skin reading chose the garment and that every render has a receipt, over the one run where neither is true. The agentic engine, meanwhile, has no deterministic fallback on the exact path an unlocked judge defaults to — the demo-can't-fail rule is violated precisely where the highest-value visitor lands. Priorities are not close. Items 1 and 2 (upload, file) are HUMAN, take under an hour together, and change the pass/fail. Item 3 (unlock redirect) and item 4 (agentic fallback) are one-line and ten-line fixes standing between a judge and a working experience. Items 5 and 6 are the integrity edits that must land before the entry goes in. Then, for the tiebreaker, items 7 and 8: draw the chain and put the causal edge on screen with a why-this-garment chip that is honest when the wardrobe overrides the colour read. Stop building. Ship, then correct, then decorate. The single weakest link is unchanged in shape and worse in irony than in review 002: the evidence a skeptical judge would need now exists, is machine-checkable, and is locked in a drawer three days from the deadline.
